papers.title: What Matters In On-Policy Reinforcement Learning? A Large-Scale Empirical Study
papers.authors_short: Andrychowicz, Raichuk, Stańczyk, Orsini et al.
papers.venue: ICLR 2021 (published there as 'What Matters for On-Policy Deep Actor-Critic Methods? A Large-Scale Study')
papers.code_status: no code link in the arXiv record or paper text
papers.api_title: What Matters In On-Policy Reinforcement Learning? A Large-Scale Empirical Study
papers.core_idea: Trains over 250,000 agents on five MuJoCo tasks, varying more than 50 on-policy choices with 3 seeds each. Observation normalisation, initial action std, last-layer scale, value normalisation, discount and transitions per iteration matter most; std parameterisation and advantage normalisation barely matter.
papers.what_to_take: Make observation normalisation the baseline. Sweep initial std {0.5, 1.0} with a 100x-smaller last policy layer, and tanh vs clip. Test value normalisation per task. Keep advantage normalisation. Skip state-dependent std.
papers.left_untested: Single-agent MuJoCo, 1-2M steps, 3 seeds per configuration. Tanh vs clip was tested without an entropy bonus. No [0,1] muscle actuators, shared multi-agent critic, staged training or actor freezing.
papers.feasibility_notes: Paper only. Each recommendation maps to an SB3 or CleanRL flag; one ablation arm costs about one SMAT stage per seed.

papers.title: The 37 Implementation Details of Proximal Policy Optimization
papers.code_status: public (last push 2024-03); the reference CleanRL (github.com/vwxyzjn/cleanrl; JMLR 23(274) 2022, arXiv 2111.08819) is active, last push 2026-04
papers.api_title: The 37 Implementation Details of Proximal Policy Optimization
papers.core_idea: Line-by-line audit of openai/baselines PPO listing 37 details. Continuous-control defaults: state-independent log-std initialised at 0, actions clipped for the env but stored unclipped, running observation normalisation clipped to ±10, reward scaling, value-loss clipping, truncation not bootstrapped.
papers.what_to_take: Use as the checklist for every unspecified SMAT flag. Record whether obs/reward normalisation, value clipping and truncation bootstrapping are on (SB3 and CleanRL defaults differ). Always log approx-KL and clipfrac.
papers.left_untested: Documents defaults rather than measuring their effects. Nothing on multi-agent critics or bounded [0,1] muscle actions, and no effect sizes for most continuous-control details.
papers.feasibility_notes: Free to read. CleanRL's single-file PPO is a readable base for a two-actor, shared-critic variant.

papers.title: Where Entropy Is Measured Matters: Policy Geometry in Bounded Continuous-Control PPO
papers.code_status: paper promises an archival package (MyoLeg/SB3 and Dog/CleanRL code, hashed checkpoints); no public URL found 2026-09-23
papers.api_title: Where Entropy Is Measured Matters: Policy Geometry in Bounded Continuous-Control PPO
papers.core_idea: In an 80-muscle MyoLeg task using SB3 PPO (entropy coefficient 1e-3), a clipped Gaussian put 89% of muscle commands within 5% of a bound and 82% of means outside [0,1]. With tanh policies, executed-action entropy H(a) cut near-bound occupancy from 71% (latent H(u)) to 19%.
papers.what_to_take: Log each actor's near-bound occupancy (|a-bound|<0.05) and the fraction of means outside bounds. Sweep entropy space {latent H(u) (SB3 default), none, executed H(a)} at SMAT's 0.001/0.003 coefficients.
papers.left_untested: Three seeds per condition, one MyoLeg model plus Dog-Stand. More interior actions did not raise return. No exoskeleton co-adaptation, Beta policies, or gait/metabolic outcomes.
papers.feasibility_notes: Directly reproducible in MyoAssist/SB3: changing the entropy space is a few lines in the loss, and occupancy logging costs nothing.

papers.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of PPO in Cooperative, Multi-Agent Games
papers.authors_short: Yu, Velu, Vinitsky, Gao, Wang, Bayen, Wu
papers.api_title: The Surprising Effectiveness of PPO in Cooperative, Multi-Agent Games
papers.core_idea: Ablates PPO factors in cooperative multi-agent games (MPE, SMAC, GRF, Hanabi). Value-target normalisation never hurt and often helped. Critic inputs that combine global and agent-specific features won. Fewer epochs, no minibatch splitting, clip below 0.2 and large batches worked best.
papers.what_to_take: Adopt running value-target normalisation in the shared critic. Give the critic global state plus agent-specific features. Sweep epochs {5,10,20} and minibatches {1,4}: SMAT's 20 epochs x 4 minibatches exceeds MAPPO's advice.
papers.left_untested: Discrete cooperative games with homogeneous agents. No continuous musculoskeletal control, heterogeneous human and device actors, staged freezing, or target-KL early stopping interacting with epoch count.
papers.feasibility_notes: Every factor is a flag. The epoch/minibatch sweep costs about 6 arms x seeds of CPU time on the EPYC.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
papers.code_status: public, Apache-2.0, archived read-only since 2024; still pip-installable
papers.api_title: Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
papers.core_idea: With 3-10 runs, point estimates mislead. Report stratified-bootstrap interval estimates, IQM instead of mean or median, performance profiles and probability of improvement. Percentile CIs hold from about 10 runs. Max-over-training protocols are not comparable with final-performance results.
papers.what_to_take: Run at least 10 seeds per sweep arm. Report IQM of final-window return with 95% percentile-bootstrap CIs and probability of improvement over the SMAT-default arm. Never mix max-checkpoint and final-checkpoint numbers.
papers.left_untested: Validated mainly on Atari 100k and multi-task aggregates. Single-task SMAT comparisons lose the stratification benefit. Staged training and correlated evaluation episodes within a run are not treated.
papers.feasibility_notes: pip install rliable; each analysis takes seconds of CPU.

papers.title: Empirical Design in Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_status: no code link in the arXiv record
papers.core_idea: Practical guide to RL experiments: performance measures, tolerance vs confidence intervals, number of runs, hypothesis tests, and maximisation bias in hyperparameter selection. Long-tailed run distributions needed about 20-30 runs, and maximising over configurations inflates reported performance.
papers.what_to_take: Use their two-stage workflow: sweep on tuning seeds, then re-run chosen configs on fresh seeds and report only those (bootstrapped variant if affordable). Flag winners at sweep-range edges. Report tolerance intervals.
papers.left_untested: Worked examples are small classic-control and DQN tasks. No compute recipe for expensive 100M-step runs, staged curricula or multi-agent co-adaptation.
papers.feasibility_notes: Paper only. The protocol costs extra seeds, not new code.

papers.title: Implementation Matters in Deep Policy Gradients: A Case Study on PPO and TRPO
papers.authors_short: Engstrom, Ilyas, Santurkar, Tsipras, Janoos, Rudolph, Madry
papers.api_title: Implementation Matters in Deep Policy Gradients: A Case Study on PPO and TRPO
papers.core_idea: Code-level optimisations in reference PPO (value clipping, reward scaling, orthogonal init, Adam annealing) explain most of PPO's gain over TRPO. Reward normalisation, annealing and initialisation significantly shifted Humanoid and Walker2d reward. Clipping alone did not keep probability ratios inside the trust region.
papers.what_to_take: Treat reward scaling, orthogonal init and lr annealing as sweep factors, not constants. Log the max probability ratio and KL per update to confirm clip 0.15 and target-KL 0.01 really bound policy change.
papers.left_untested: Ablation grid on two MuJoCo tasks, 5 seeds, 2019-era baselines. No bounded muscle actions, multi-agent critics, KL early stopping or observation-normalisation ablation in the main grid.
papers.feasibility_notes: The ablation grid is cheap to mirror with SB3 flags on short runs.

papers.title: Stable-Baselines3: Reliable Reinforcement Learning Implementations
papers.authors_short: Raffin, Hill, Gleave, Kanervisto, Ernestus, Dormann
papers.code_status: public, MIT, active (last push 2026-09-09, master 2.9.2a0); PPO source checked 2026-09-23
papers.core_idea: Tested PyTorch RL library that MyoAssist's rl_train subclasses. In current PPO source, n_steps is per environment, sampled Gaussian actions are clipped only for the env, timeouts bootstrap, and target_kl stops all remaining epochs once a minibatch's approx-KL exceeds 1.5x target.
papers.what_to_take: Read SMAT's '2048 steps' as per env: 65,536 samples per update in 4 minibatches of 16,384. SB3 defaults: no VecNormalize, log_std_init 0, clip_range_vf None, advantage normalisation on.
papers.left_untested: Library paper with no ablations. Its defaults (no observation or reward normalisation) differ from CleanRL and baselines and were not benchmarked for musculoskeletal or multi-agent PPO.
papers.feasibility_notes: Already a MyoAssist dependency, so there is no porting cost.

papers.title: On the Mistaken Assumption of Interchangeable Deep Reinforcement Learning Implementations
papers.venue: ICSE 2025 (IEEE/ACM 47th Int. Conf. on Software Engineering)
papers.code_status: archived artifact on Zenodo (link from paper)
papers.api_title: On the Mistaken Assumption of Interchangeable Deep Reinforcement Learning Implementations
papers.core_idea: Differential testing of five PPO implementations on 56 Atari games with matched hyperparameters: three reached superhuman scores in about 50% of trials, two in under 15%. Code-level inconsistencies, including timeout handling and value clipping, were implicated, and interchanging implementations flipped a replicated study's conclusion.
papers.what_to_take: Pin one PPO codebase and version for all SMAT arms. Never compare runs across libraries. When porting, diff timeout bootstrapping, value clipping and KL-stopping semantics against SB3 first.
papers.left_untested: Discrete Atari only. No continuous or bounded actions, no multi-agent critics, and no measure of which single inconsistency drives continuous-control gaps.
papers.feasibility_notes: A differential check is cheap: two codebases x 10 seeds on one short SMAT stage.

papers.title: Preventing Learning Stagnation in PPO by Scaling to 1 Million Parallel Environments
papers.authors_short: Beukman, Khetarpal, Zheng, Dabney, Foerster, Dennis, Lyle
papers.venue: RLC 2026 (accepted); arXiv v1 Mar 2026, v2 Jul 2026
papers.code_status: none found (paper text and first author's GitHub checked 2026-09-23)
papers.api_title: Preventing Learning Stagnation in PPO by Scaling to 1 Million Parallel Environments
papers.core_idea: Models PPO's outer loop as noisy stochastic optimisation. Plateaus arise when the policy step size (set by regularisation strength and epochs) is too large for the gradient noise (set by samples per update). Tuning Adam's learning rate cannot fix this, but more parallel samples can.
papers.what_to_take: Treat per-env vs aggregate counting as a 32x change in samples per update. When scaling samples, keep minibatch size and learning rate fixed and add optimisation steps. Sweep epochs {5,10,20} jointly with rollout size.
papers.left_untested: Evidence comes from JAX 2D physics (Kinetix, procedural locomotion) and IsaacGym dexterous-hand tasks. No musculoskeletal tasks, multi-agent critics, or CPU-bound 32-env regimes like SMAT.
papers.feasibility_notes: The principle applies at 32-64 envs. Million-env results need GPU simulation, which MyoAssist lacks.

papers.title: Performance Variation in Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.api_title: Performance Variation in Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.core_idea: Argues that confidence intervals on the mean hide run-to-run variation. Proposes min-max IPR-90 (normalised 5th-95th percentile range) and run-wise percentile plots, using 100 runs per task on 59 MuJoCo/DMC tasks. PPO varied more than SAC, and LayerNorm narrowed PPO's variation.
papers.what_to_take: Report min-max IPR-90 of final return for each SMAT arm next to IQM CIs. When means tie, prefer the arm with lower spread. Test LayerNorm in actors and critic as a variance-reduction arm.
papers.left_untested: Single-agent, no parallel environments, 10M-step PPO. The 100 runs per task are unaffordable for 100M-step SMAT stages. No staged or multi-agent training.
papers.feasibility_notes: The statistic is trivial to compute, but reliable 5th and 95th percentiles need many seeds (the paper used 100).

papers.title: Improving Stochastic Policy Gradients in Continuous Control with Deep Reinforcement Learning using the Beta Distribution
papers.code_status: none linked on the PMLR page
papers.api_title: Improving Stochastic Policy Gradients in Continuous Control with Deep Reinforcement Learning using the Beta Distribution
papers.core_idea: Clipping an infinite-support Gaussian to bounded actions biases the policy gradient. A Beta policy has finite support, is bias-free, and converged faster with TRPO and ACER on Gym/MuJoCo continuous-control tasks.
papers.what_to_take: Add a Beta-policy arm for the 26 muscle excitations ([0,1] support) and a rescaled Beta for exo torques. Compare it with clipped and tanh Gaussians at equal steps and seeds.
papers.left_untested: Tested with TRPO and ACER, not PPO with clipping and target-KL. No high-dimensional muscle actuation. He et al. 2026 did not test Beta, so its boundary geometry is untested.
papers.feasibility_notes: SB3 has no Beta distribution. Needs a custom Distribution subclass; torch.distributions.Beta covers sampling and log-prob.

papers.title: How Many Random Seeds? Statistical Power Analysis in Deep Reinforcement Learning Experiments
papers.api_title: How Many Random Seeds? Statistical Power Analysis in Deep Reinforcement Learning Experiments
papers.core_idea: Tutorial linking seed count to type-I and type-II errors for Welch's t-test and bootstrap tests. Two runs of the identical DDPG algorithm with 5 seeds each were declared significantly different. Bootstrap tests need at least 20 samples, and power analysis underestimates the seeds required.
papers.what_to_take: Run a pilot of at least 20 seeds of the SMAT-default config to estimate run-to-run SD. Size each comparison by power analysis (Welch's t-test, alpha<=0.05, corrected for the number of arms) and round N up.
papers.left_untested: Single-task HalfCheetah examples. No guidance for many-arm sweeps sharing a baseline, sequential testing, or staged training where early stages gate later ones.
papers.feasibility_notes: The formulas and code are trivial; the 20-seed pilot is the real cost.

papers.title: A Method for Evaluating Hyperparameter Sensitivity in Reinforcement Learning
papers.api_title: A Method for Evaluating Hyperparameter Sensitivity in Reinforcement Learning
papers.core_idea: Defines hyperparameter sensitivity across a set of environments and applies it to PPO normalisation variants over 4.3M runs on Brax MuJoCo. Advantage normalisations raised tuned performance but also sensitivity. Symlog value targets lowered performance, and observation normalisation may slightly reduce sensitivity.
papers.what_to_take: When sweeping observation, value and advantage normalisation, re-tune lr in each arm (at least {3e-5, 5e-5, 1e-4}), since a fixed-lr comparison can misattribute gains. Keep per-minibatch advantage normalisation on.
papers.left_untested: Single-agent Brax tasks on short budgets. Running value-target normalisation (PopArt-style), bounded muscle actions and multi-agent shared critics were not included.
papers.feasibility_notes: The method is analysis only. Applying it means a small lr grid per arm, multiplying runs by 3-5.

papers.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
papers.core_idea: Defines the clipped surrogate, optimised for K epochs on minibatches drawn from N actors x T timesteps. MuJoCo defaults: T=2048 per actor, 10 epochs, minibatch 64, Adam 3e-4, gamma 0.99, lambda 0.95, learned std, no entropy bonus, 3 seeds.
papers.what_to_take: Algorithm 1 requires minibatch M <= N*T. SMAT's 16,384 minibatch only fits 2,048 steps per env (N*T = 65,536), so adopt per-env counting as the primary reading.
papers.left_untested: No ablation of normalisation, action bounding, value clipping or seed count. One million steps with 3 seeds per task.

papers.title: Learning values across many orders of magnitude
papers.authors_short: van Hasselt, Guez, Hessel, Mnih, Silver
papers.api_title: Learning values across many orders of magnitude
papers.core_idea: PopArt adaptively normalises learning targets with running mean and scale (ART) and rescales the output layer to preserve unnormalised predictions (POP). Value estimates then survive abrupt changes in return magnitude without reward clipping.
papers.what_to_take: For the shared critic across SMAT's four stages, sweep {no value normalisation, running target normalisation, PopArt}. PopArt should matter most at stage switches, where reward terms and return scale jump.
papers.left_untested: Motivated by and shown on value-based Atari learning. Never tested with PPO in staged multi-agent continuous control or with actor freezing.
papers.feasibility_notes: About a critic-head's worth of code; SB3 has no built-in PopArt or value-target normalisation.

cluster_lessons: Transition counting is almost certainly per environment. PPO's Algorithm 1 requires minibatch <= N*T, and SB3 and CleanRL both define n_steps per env. A 16,384 minibatch cannot fit an aggregate 2,048-step rollout. Per-env gives 65,536 samples per update, 4 minibatches and up to 80 gradient steps per update before target-KL stopping.

Picking a codebase silently picks SMAT's unspecified flags. SB3 (MyoAssist's base): no observation or reward normalisation, no value clipping, bootstraps timeouts, stops all epochs when a minibatch's approx-KL exceeds 1.5x target. CleanRL: normalises observations (clipped to ±10) and rewards, clips value loss, treats truncation as terminal, checks KL once per epoch at 1x target. Hundal et al. 2025 show such differences can flip conclusions.

Code evidence from MyoAssist HEAD b1baf69 (2026-08-25; SMAT's own code is not public): SB3 PPO subclass with SubprocVecEnv and no running observation normalisation. Actors use a tanh-bounded mean and one state-independent log_std vector spanning all human and exo action dims. log_std_init is 0.0 in the tutorial JSON but -2.0 in the dataclass default (initial std 1.0 vs 0.14).

'Freezing an actor' is under-defined. With one log_std vector shared across both actors, freezing the human network does not freeze its log-std entries unless they are masked. Under SB3's latent-entropy bonus the entropy gradient pushes every log-std up at a constant rate, so a frozen actor's exploration noise can keep growing. Specify, and log, per-actor log_std at every stage.

Expected effect sizes for the sweep. Observation normalisation was crucial on 4 of 5 MuJoCo tasks. A 100x-smaller last policy layer gave +66% on Humanoid, and tanh vs clip +30% on HalfCheetah. Value normalisation was crucial on 2 of 5 tasks and hurt on 1 (Andrychowicz). Clipped-Gaussian muscle policies sat within 5% of a bound for 89% of actions (He 2026). State-dependent vs state-independent std showed no clear effect.

Honest comparison protocol. Use at least 10 seeds per arm, or 20 for the default-config pilot that sizes power. Report IQM of the final evaluation window with 95% percentile-bootstrap CIs plus min-max IPR-90 spread, compared at equal environment steps. Re-evaluate sweep winners on fresh seeds and correct for the number of arms.

Equal budgets: fix total environment steps per arm. If an arm changes samples per update, keep minibatch size and learning rate fixed and vary optimisation steps (Beukman 2026). Report wall-clock separately, since rankings can change under wall-clock rather than sample budgets (Hamed et al. 2026, arXiv 2607.17326, verified, not selected).

Checkpoint selection: max-over-training protocols are not comparable with final-performance results, and on Atari 100k the gap exceeded real algorithm differences (Agarwal). Picking the best of many checkpoints or configs inflates scores (Patterson's maximisation bias). Fix the rule before sweeping, e.g. the mean of the last K evaluations with deterministic and stochastic policies both logged.
occupied_claims: Observation normalisation, initial action std and last-layer initialisation are among the most influential PPO continuous-control choices (Andrychowicz et al. 2021).
Code-level optimisations, not the clipped objective, explain most of PPO's advantage over TRPO, and clipping alone does not enforce the trust region (Engstrom et al. 2020).
PPO implementations with matched hyperparameters are not interchangeable and can flip study conclusions (Hundal et al. 2025).
Clipped-Gaussian PPO muscle policies in MyoLeg concentrate at action bounds, and entropy measurement space (latent vs executed) changes mean-variance geometry (He et al. 2026).
Value normalisation and critic input design strongly affect multi-agent PPO with a centralised critic; fewer epochs and less minibatching help (Yu et al. 2022).
Point estimates from 3-10 runs are unreliable; IQM with stratified bootstrap CIs and performance profiles are the recommended remedy (Agarwal et al. 2021).
Maximising over hyperparameter configurations or checkpoints inflates reported performance (Patterson et al. 2024; Agarwal et al. 2021).
PPO plateaus can come from too few samples per update relative to the policy step size, and more parallel environments fix them (Beukman et al. 2026).
Normalisation variants that raise tuned PPO performance also raise hyperparameter sensitivity (Adkins et al. 2024).
Beta policies remove the bias of clipped Gaussians on bounded actions (Chou et al. 2017).
Uncertainty in the mean understates run-to-run variation; LayerNorm narrows PPO variation (Tanaka & Mahmood 2026).
open_gaps: No study measures these PPO implementation choices in human-exoskeleton co-adaptation with two heterogeneous actors and a shared critic.
How actor freezing and staged curricula interact with log-std, entropy bonus and shared-critic value targets in PPO is unstudied.
Beta vs clipped vs tanh Gaussian has not been compared for high-dimensional muscle control under PPO with an entropy bonus (He et al. 2026 tested Gaussian variants only).
There are no published run-to-run variance estimates for 100M-step musculoskeletal PPO to size seed budgets; a pilot is required.
In the studies reviewed here, target-KL early-stopping semantics (per-minibatch 1.5x in SB3 vs per-epoch 1x in CleanRL) were not ablated at high epoch counts like SMAT's 20.
Whether observation-normalisation statistics should be frozen, reset or shared across stages and between the two actors is unaddressed.
Checkpoint-selection rules based on gait or assistance metrics rather than return have not been examined for bias.
